Frozen regression budgets (spec 089). Every number below was MEASURED first (3 runs on the baseline environment), then given headroom — never the other way round. 'hard' metrics fail 'pnpm test:performance'; 'report' metrics are recorded and printed only. Change a budget only in a PR that explains the evidence, edits docs/specs/089 and — for bundle/DOM numbers — names the dependency or template change behind it.

baselineEnvironment.note: Local-machine regression baselines, not production latency; no remote or cloud measurement exists.

metrics.rationale: first page: page query + total count. Deterministic: counted at the DatabaseAdapter boundary, independent of machine speed. The budget equals the baseline, so ANY extra query (an N+1, a second count, a per-row lookup) fails.

deep page (offset 1500): page query + total count. Deterministic: counted at the DatabaseAdapter boundary, independent of machine speed. The budget equals the baseline, so ANY extra query (an N+1, a second count, a per-row lookup) fails.

filtered page: page query + total count. Deterministic: counted at the DatabaseAdapter boundary, independent of machine speed. The budget equals the baseline, so ANY extra query (an N+1, a second count, a per-row lookup) fails.

nested and/or page: page query + total count. Deterministic: counted at the DatabaseAdapter boundary, independent of machine speed. The budget equals the baseline, so ANY extra query (an N+1, a second count, a per-row lookup) fails.

count with the nested predicate: one count. Deterministic: counted at the DatabaseAdapter boundary, independent of machine speed. The budget equals the baseline, so ANY extra query (an N+1, a second count, a per-row lookup) fails.

depth-1 page of 50: page + count + ONE lookup per relation field (author, tags, cover). Deterministic: counted at the DatabaseAdapter boundary, independent of machine speed. The budget equals the baseline, so ANY extra query (an N+1, a second count, a per-row lookup) fails.

depth-1 page of 500: identical to a page of 50 — population is batched. Deterministic: counted at the DatabaseAdapter boundary, independent of machine speed. The budget equals the baseline, so ANY extra query (an N+1, a second count, a per-row lookup) fails.

depth-1 document: one read + one lookup per relation field. Deterministic: counted at the DatabaseAdapter boundary, independent of machine speed. The budget equals the baseline, so ANY extra query (an N+1, a second count, a per-row lookup) fails.

admin list request: page query + total count. Deterministic: counted at the DatabaseAdapter boundary, independent of machine speed. The budget equals the baseline, so ANY extra query (an N+1, a second count, a per-row lookup) fails.

admin filtered list request: page query + total count. Deterministic: counted at the DatabaseAdapter boundary, independent of machine speed. The budget equals the baseline, so ANY extra query (an N+1, a second count, a per-row lookup) fails.

largest accepted where (4 KB): still page query + total count. Deterministic: counted at the DatabaseAdapter boundary, independent of machine speed. The budget equals the baseline, so ANY extra query (an N+1, a second count, a per-row lookup) fails.

over-deep where: rejected with ZERO database calls. Deterministic: counted at the DatabaseAdapter boundary, independent of machine speed. The budget equals the baseline, so ANY extra query (an N+1, a second count, a per-row lookup) fails.

upload: one storage-intent create + one atomic document batch. Deterministic: counted at the DatabaseAdapter boundary, independent of machine speed. The budget equals the baseline, so ANY extra query (an N+1, a second count, a per-row lookup) fails.

Database calls of a depth-1 page of 500 rows minus a page of 10 rows. 0 = population cost does not grow with the result (no N+1). Also asserted by the measurement itself and by packages/runtime/src/query-work-bounds.test.ts.
DOM nodes the admin list creates for 50 rows. Deterministic (identical in every run). ~10% headroom absorbs small template changes; template bloat beyond that is a review decision, not an accident.
DOM nodes the admin list creates for 500 rows. Deterministic (identical in every run). ~10% headroom absorbs small template changes; template bloat beyond that is a review decision, not an accident.
10x the rows should cost ~5.6x (fixed per-request overhead + linear row work). The budget (12) fails only a super-linear population or hydration cost.
metrics.sensitivity: low (both terms measured on the same machine in the same run)

metrics.rationale: Paging to offset 1500 costs the same as page 1 (indexed sort). Budget 5x catches a regression to materialising the skipped rows.
metrics.sensitivity: low (both terms measured on the same machine in the same run)

metrics.rationale: A 3-level nested predicate costs ~1.5x an unfiltered page. Budget 6x catches pathological predicate translation.
metrics.sensitivity: low (both terms measured on the same machine in the same run)

metrics.rationale: 10x the rows renders in ~8.7x the time (linear). Budget 20x fails a quadratic list (e.g. an O(n^2) track/identity or per-row lookup).
metrics.sensitivity: low (both terms measured on the same machine in the same run)

metrics.rationale: Growth of the garbage-collected JS heap across the second half of six repetitions of the same operation mix (~480 operations). Steady state is 0; a leak of >=10 KB per operation exceeds 5 MB. Heap readings follow an explicit GC, so they are stable.
JS heap after fixture load and six workload rounds (baseline ~25 MB). Release-blocker ceiling 100 MB (4x); above 45 MB (1.8x) is a review signal. A gross-regression guard, not a precision budget.

Process RSS after the workload (baseline ~395 MB, dominated by the native libSQL driver and allocator behaviour: RSS moves up AND down between identical runs and with the raw adapter alone — spec 089). Only a 1 GB ceiling is gated; 700 MB is a review signal. Never use RSS deltas as a trend.
